assessment: Insecticides have been implicated in the decline of beneficial insect species. The organic insecticide Spinosad has emerged as a alternative to synthetic insecticides and is thought to be less harmful to beneficial insects than synthetic insecticides. This article used the insect model Drosophila to analyze the impact of Spinosad. It reveals that low doses of Spinosad antagonize its neuronal target, the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit alpha 6, affecting the physiology of Drosophila. This study reveals that although being organic and assumed to be less harmful, spinosad can have profound impact on non-target insects.
